newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jilin sees little improvement in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Jilin sees little improvement in 1997.

text.p: Petrochemical giant Jilin Chemical Industrial Co Ltd does not expect to see an improvement in the petrochemical industry in China before 1998, a senior executive said on Tuesday.

"We believe there is little room for prices to fall further, but at present we haven't seen signs of a recovery," said Lu Qi Rong, secretary of the boad and company deputy director at a news conference on Tuesday.
"We believe that we will not see evidence of an improvement in 1997," Lu added.
Lu said analysis of the industry pointed to a recovery in 1998.

Jilin Chemical reported profit attributable to shareholders of 311.80 million yuan (US$37.57 million) in 1996 according to international accounting standards. This was a 58.2 percent decline over the previous year.
Earnings per share fell to 0.09 yuan in 1996 from 0.25 yuan, a decline of 64 percent.
Despite a weak market, the company managed to increase its sales, and turnover rose 8.5 percent to 7.68 billion yuan.
In the first half of the year, the company reported profitable to shareholders of 337.95 million yuan.

The reasons for the poor second-half results were the costs incurred in the start of trial production at new facilities, all part of the company's Ethylene Project and the closure of other facilities for regular maintenance, said Lu.
Financing costs also rose to 231.98 million yuan in 1996, compared with 174.12 million in 1995, the company's annual report showed.

Jilin, like Yizheng Chemical Fibre Co Ltd and Shanghai Petrochemical Co Ltd, suffered in 1996 from declines in the sales prices of its chemical products and a rise in the price of crude, the main raw material used in production.

The prices for three of the company's five principal products, petrochemical and organic chemical products, dyestuff and dye intermediates and synthetic rubber, fell by 14 percent, 16 percent and 12 percent, the company's annual report said.
However, while the prices of the company products were not likely to rise much in the current year, increases in raw materials costs would be limited in 1997, Lu said.
"The crude price (paid by the company) is likely to rise to US$20.00 per barrel," said Lu, adding that he thought domestic prices would reach international levels in the near future.
In late December 1996, the government raised the price of class one crude oil to 1,005 yuan per tonne from 885 yuan, but left the price of class two unchanged at 1,280 yuan per tonne
In 1996, the state raised the price of domestically produced class I (crude) oil to 885 yuan per tonne from 754 yuan and reduced the price of class two oil to 1,280 yuan per tonne from 1,310 yuan.
The overall weighted average crude price paid by the group in 1996 was 1,057 yuan per tonne.
This increase was chiefly responsible for a 23 percent rise in the company's cost of sales.
The company's future earnings growth will in large part be determined by the success of the large ethylene project currently under construction.
By the end of 1996, the Jilin group, including the listed company and its parent company, would have invested a total of 6.6 billion yuan in the Ethylene Project, Lu said.
The H share gained HK$0.04 to close at HK$1.03 on Tuesday.
